description: Adaptive Surface 0.12.0 projects native transition pixels onto matching upper surface boundaries using transient non-interactive model entities, independently for four sides.
changes: Prepare shared 128x128 upper-face native-mask atlases and source tint before admission; 32 native pixels per axis preserved.
Require two Adaptive Surfaces, matching whole edge heights and local plane normals, plus an original donor group/tag relationship.
Rotate north-edge models/textures for N/E/S/W; permit continuous slopes across a cell height.
Reconcile active section surfaces every 0.5 seconds; retain unchanged visuals and reconstruct non-serialized overlays after loading.
Use native Intangible and no interaction/hit/collision components, preserving F and decorative attachments.
advantages: No placement-time common asset registration, new block states or block atlas refresh
Existing selected materials and approved geometry remain byte-identical
Original native transition silhouettes instead of invented blend pairs
disadvantages: Active-surface scans and per-edge entities add work; no large-world performance benchmark
